samples.summary: `keepDirty` turns an `undefined` dirty set (= "recompute everything") into an EMPTY set (= "trust the cache for everything"), weakening invalidation for writes made later in the same undo unit
samples.evidence: `dirtyBlockIds = opts?.keepDirty ? (priorDirty ?? new Set()) : undefined;`. `computeLayout` only consults `layoutCache` while the set is non-null, so `undefined` means a full re-measure and an empty Set means none. Inside `TextEditor.withUndoUnit`, the first interior `requestRender()` now runs `recomputeLayout({keepDirty:true})`, which replaces the `undefined` left by `invalidateLayout()` with an empty Set *and* rebuilds `layoutCache`. Any store write made after that point in the same unit that does not call `markDirty()`/`invalidateLayout()` is therefore skipped by the unit's final paint, where before the change it was picked up by the full recompute. Reachable: `insertPlainText()` (text-editor.ts:4346) calls `ensureEditableBlock()` and `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge()` — both write without marking dirty — and it runs after `deleteSelection()` has already triggered an interior render (e.g. `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`, text-editor.ts:4322). Contained: the final `recomputeLayout()` resets the set to `undefined`, so the next render self-corrects; the artefact is one stale painted frame.

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.batch()`: an *adopted* checkpoint that the body materialized and then reverted is left on `undoStack` while `redoStack` is restored, producing a dead Cmd+Z and an undo/redo pair taken from two different branches
samples.evidence: In the `wroteNothing` arm the pop is gated on `if (!adopted)`. When `adopted` is true and the body wrote and then reverted itself, `willWrite()` has already pushed `before` onto `undoStack`, so the guard skips the pop and the checkpoint stays — a checkpoint byte-identical to the current document, i.e. an undo press that changes nothing. At the same time `this.redoStack = priorRedo` restores redo entries that belong to the pre-batch branch, so after the dead undo the redo stack holds `[...priorRedo, currentDoc]` — two unrelated branches stacked. The adjacent comment only justifies keeping an adopted checkpoint that is still *pending* (the `handleBackspace` shape), not one that has already been materialized.

samples.summary: First-load while offline renders "Link unavailable" instead of the loader, because react-query v5's `isLoading` is false for a *paused* fetch
samples.evidence: `if (token && isLoading) return <Loader />;` then `if (!token || fatal || !resolved)` renders the terminal "Link unavailable / Invalid or expired link" screen. In @tanstack/react-query v5 (packages/frontend/package.json:56) `isLoading === isPending && isFetching`; with the default `networkMode: 'online'` an initial fetch made while offline is *paused* (`fetchStatus: 'paused'`, `isFetching: false`), so `isLoading` is false, `resolved` is undefined and no error has been produced — the component falls straight through to the failure screen. That is exactly the "a request that got no answer must not be treated as a verdict" rule the rest of the change is built around (`isRevokedShareLinkError`), violated for the very first resolve. Self-corrects once connectivity returns and the paused fetch resumes.

samples.summary: `neuterMutations` replaces the async members `paste`/`insertImage` with a synchronous no-op returning `undefined`, so promise-chaining on a disposed editor throws
samples.evidence: `const noop = () => {}; for (const name of MUTATING_METHODS) (api as ... )[name] = noop;` with the comment "`paste`/`insertImage` are async (Promise<void>) … A bare no-op satisfies both — callers only await or ignore." `await undefined` and `void x()` are fine, but `editor.paste().then(...)`/`.catch(...)`/`.finally(...)` is a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. This was previously only reachable on a read-only mount; `dispose()` now applies the same neutering to every editable editor, widening the set of callers that can hit it. Returning `Promise.resolve()` for those two names would close it.

samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the mount effect deps discards the session's Yorkie undo history on every role flip, because the rebuilt `YorkieDocStore` re-arms its undo floor at the current stack depth
samples.evidence: The effect now re-runs on a `readOnly` change, constructing `const store = new YorkieDocStore(doc)` (line 356). `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor calls `markUndoFloor()`, which records the *current* top of `doc.history`'s undo stack as the boundary users may not undo past. Since the Yorkie document survives the rebuild (it belongs to the enclosing `DocumentProvider`), every edit the user made before the flip is now below the new floor and `canUndo()` refuses it. Harmless for a downgrade to viewer (no undo UI), but a `viewer` → `editor` upgrade — equally reachable through the periodic share-link re-resolve — silently strands the session's prior undo history, along with caret/selection/scroll state.

samples.summary: `writePageSetup` still writes through the raw `docStore`, bypassing `revocableStore`, so the "disposed editor cannot write" invariant depends on the ruler being torn down rather than on the revocable handle
samples.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` was changed to go through `revocableStore` (line 3321) specifically to close the page-setup hole, but `writePageSetup` (line 2325, reached by `ruler.onMarginChange` and `EditorAPI.setPageSetup`) still calls `docStore.setPageSetup(...)` on the raw store. Same for `docStore.applyStyles(...)` at line 1379 and the `docStore.setDocStyles/updateStyleDefinition/resetStyle/resetAllStyles` calls at 3576-3627. All of these are reachable today only through `api` members that `neuterMutations` replaces, or through ruler callbacks that `ruler.dispose()` unwires, so nothing is currently exploitable — but the revocable handle is not what is protecting them, which is the opposite of what the surrounding comments claim, and a new non-`api` caller of any of them would reopen a write path on a disposed editor.

searchedFor: Read text-editor.ts:2760-2860 to confirm the keyboard twins were batched
Read yorkie-doc-store.ts:2960-3022 (withUpdate / batch = one doc.update per write)
finding.summary: Toolbar block-level mutators (`applyBlockStyle`, `toggleList`, `indent`, `outdent`) still write once per selected block with no `doc.batch()`, so the #1045 data loss this change fixes for the keyboard paths survives on the toolbar
finding.evidence:
This change batched the TextEditor keyboard twins — `handleTab` (text-editor.ts:2772), `handleIndent` (2820), `handleOutdent` (2844) — and the toolbar's inline-style path (`applyStyleImpl`, editor.ts:1260/1267). But the sibling `EditorAPI` members in editor.ts are untouched and still loop `forEachBlockInSelection` with a store write inside and no batch:

- `applyBlockStyle` (editor.ts:3451-3455): `docStore.snapshot(); forEachBlockInSelection(block => doc.applyBlockStyle(block.id, style));`
- `toggleList` (3612-3624): `doc.setBlockType(...)` per block
- `indent` (3632-3649) and `outdent` (3656-3674): `doc.setBlockType(...)` / `doc.applyBlockStyle(...)` per block

Each `doc.*` call is one `store` write, and on `YorkieDocStore` one write outside a batch is one `doc.update()` and therefore one undo-stack entry (`withUpdate`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:2972-2980). That is exactly the shape the new `withUndoUnit` doc comment describes: past Yorkie's 50-entry `MaxUndoRedoStackDepth` `pushUndo` shifts the OLDEST entries off, so over a >50-block selection the earliest blocks' change becomes permanently un-undoable.

All four are reachable from normal UI, not internal-only: `editor.applyBlockStyle({ alignment })` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:566, 743), `editor.applyBlockStyle({ lineHeight })` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:517), `editor?.toggleList(...)` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:941/945, text-paragraph-group.tsx:176/194), `editor?.indent()/outdent()` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:949/953, text-paragraph-group.tsx:212/230).

Net effect: pressing Tab batches, clicking the identical Increase-indent toolbar button does not — and the new frontend test file only pins the keyboard variants plus `editor.applyStyle`, so nothing catches it. Same untouched shape at editor.ts:3702 (`insertLink` cell-range → `applyStyleToCellRange` unbatched) and editor.ts:4243-4254 (`applyTableCellStyle` cell-range loop, one write per cell).

verdict.reason: The finding claims the toolbar block-level mutators in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts write once per selected block with no doc.batch(). The code says otherwise at every cited location: applyBlockStyle (editor.ts:3459-3475) wraps its forEachBlockInSelection loop in doc.batch(); toggleList (3629-3644), indent (3652-3673) and outdent (3680-3702) each do the same, with comments explicitly referencing issue #1045 and the keyboard twins. The two "same untouched shape" sites are also batched: insertLink's cell-range branch (3734, doc.batch(() => applyStyleToCellRange(...))) and applyTableCellStyle's cell-range double loop (4297-4303). Doc.batch delegates to DocStore.batch (model/document.ts:146-148), the same grouping seam TextEditor.withUndoUnit uses (text-editor.ts:3894-3897), so each of these is one undo unit regardless of selection size. Single counterexample suffices; six are present.
